ety.text: A presumably 'natural' exclamation, attested in writing since 1921. Related to or a variation of whoops (itself attested since 1933). A shortening of whoops-a-daisy, whoopsie-daisy, or oops-a-daisy, which in turn is a mispronunciation of ups-a-daisy or upsy-daisy.

senses.d: Used to acknowledge a small mistake or accident.
ex: Oops! I left the lid off the ketchup.
Oops, I did it again / I played with your heart, got lost in the game

senses.d: Used to indicate mild surprise or shock.
A minor mistake or unforeseen difficulty.
ex: It's an oops, but one that's your fault, not your puppy's.
Every plan and every activity has an “oops.” Oops, we forgot to..., oops, who was supposed to do that? We all have experienced “oopses”.

senses.d: To make a mistake; to blunder.

grp.label: used sarcastically to acknowledge a major mistake

ety.text: Compare Spanish ops, Portuguese ops, English oops.

es:vaya.gl: expresses surprise: wow!, why, oh!, whoa!, well!, man!, boy!

es:ops.gl: acknowledgment of a minor mistake, oops

ety.text: Natural exclamation. Compare Portuguese ops, Italian ops, English oops.
